title: Symmetry, invariance and ideal restriction of the Killing form
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-Lie algebra [def-wf-lie-algebra]. Put $B_{\mathfrak g}(x,y)=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\operatorname{ad}x\circ\operatorname{ad}y)$, where $\operatorname{ad}x(z)=[x,z]$. Then
$$B_{\mathfrak g}(x,y)=B_{\mathfrak g}(y,x),\qquad B_{\mathfrak g}([x,y],z)=B_{\mathfrak g}(x,[y,z])$$
for all $x,y,z\in\mathfrak g$. For every ideal $I\subseteq\mathfrak g$ and $x,y\in I$, the Killing form of the Lie algebra $I$ satisfies
$$B_I(x,y)=B_{\mathfrak g}(x,y).$$
